questions.stem: To prove two vectors are parallel using vector geometry, you need to show that:

options.text: One is a scalar multiple of the other
They start from the same point

questions.explanation: Two vectors are parallel if and only if one is a scalar multiple of the other, i.e. $\mathbf{v} = k\mathbf{u}$ for some scalar $k$. If the vectors also share a common point, the points are collinear.
